question: Should exec, process, node-host, and active-process results use pattern-based redaction by default, with exact raw output unavailable unless a separately reviewed reveal mechanism is added later?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but only maintainers responsible for the execution security boundary can choose whether reducing secret exposure outweighs byte-exact diagnostic compatibility.

options.title: Accept redacted-by-default
options.body: After exact-head runtime proof, merge the security-first default and consider any raw-reveal capability in a separate security-reviewed proposal.

options.title: Require reveal design first
options.body: Pause this PR until it includes a narrowly authorized and audited way to retrieve exact raw output when masking prevents legitimate diagnosis.

options.title: Preserve raw output
options.body: Decline this direction if exact command-output fidelity must remain the default despite the documented agent-context exposure.

recommendation.title: Accept redacted-by-default
recommendation.body: After exact-head runtime proof, merge the security-first default and consider any raw-reveal capability in a separate security-reviewed proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged shared-redaction work is the nearest current-main ownership signal for the security contract this PR extends.
